name: Kosovo
summary: Kosovo had 1,457 battery-electric passenger cars at the end of 2025 (Eurostat), 51% more than a year earlier, and imports are rising fast: 780 electric cars came in during January–August 2026, 665 of them from China. Electric cars get no tax break — they pay the same 10% customs duty, 18% VAT and excise as combustion cars. The main public network, ECHARGE, publishes its prices: €0.39–0.49 per kWh on DC and €0.21 (day) / €0.19 (night) on AC. At home, night-rate electricity costs about 4.2 euro cents per kWh with VAT.

subsidies.note: Electric cars pay 10% customs duty, 18% VAT and excise by age like combustion cars. The Chamber of Commerce has asked to remove the duty and cut VAT to 8%; no decision so far.

buildings.text: We found no EV-specific rule for chargers in apartment buildings in Kosovo.

policy.text: The Energy Strategy 2022–2031 sets no numeric targets for electric vehicles or charging stations.
Prishtina's 2021 e-taxi licensing requires DC chargers of at least 50 kW, including one public charger per operator.

gaps: ERO's tariff decision is a scanned PDF; figures come from media.
It is not stated whether ECHARGE prices include VAT or which sites get €0.39 vs €0.49.
The share of GB/T connectors among imported Chinese EVs is not documented.
No fast charger on the R6 or R7 motorways was confirmed.
